:::{#sol-fundamental-subspaces-practice}

Here $\tp{\matr{A}}\vecf{y} = (y_1 + y_2, y_1 + y_2)$,
so $(1, -1, 0)$ is in $\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}})$.
But

$$
\vecf{b} \cdot (1, -1, 0) = 1 - 2 + 0 = -1 \neq 0,
$$

so $\vecf{b}$ is not in $\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}})^\perp = \mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$,
and $\matr{A}\vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$ has no solution.
Directly, the first two entries of $\matr{A}\vecf{x}$ are both $x_1 + x_2$,
while those of $\vecf{b}$ are $1$ and $2$.

:::
